description: Quality thresholds and the publication gate. Rules are matched in order (first match wins, fnmatch patterns). A blocking rule whose metric fails or cannot be measured blocks publication. A rule no check produced a metric for is reported as not measured. See docs/10-quality-gate.md.

rules.why: scripts/check_data_integrity.py is the existing CI gate; it includes the reporting-population and dashboard-total reconciliation (integrity.reporting-population, integrity.dashboard-totals-reconcile). A wrong published total is worse than no page.

Labels are ground truth. A database that contradicts known outcomes is publishing events known to be junk or splitting known incidents. Two are tolerated for a disputed label awaiting review; more means a cleaning step regressed or was not run.
Per-label-set breakdown of labels.contradictions_total.

The review's acceptance cases (evaluation/review_acceptance_cases.csv) and the owner's manual validation exceptions (ValidationExceptions): fragments of one incident that must be one event, victims that must be named, and events that must be out of scope. A warning, not a gate: it measures how far the rules have come.
Trend only.
Cases whose event no longer exists or cannot be traced.
Labels whose item no longer exists or whose merge cannot be followed; the regression check has no power over them.

Fixed cases for the deterministic merge rule, records-affected validation, fact recomputation and date provenance. A wrong answer means the code (or a library under it) changed behaviour the published numbers rely on.
A future-dated incident belongs to no reporting period and silently disappears from every chart and export.
A date that is not YYYY-MM-DD falls outside every half-open period query, so the incident vanishes from time-based charts.
Dates before 1990 are extraction errors; reported for repair (not charted, as the dashboard starts in 2020).
Undated incidents are counted but cannot be charted; `dedup_admin.py redate` recovers most.
Month-only placeholders make reporting lag look like repeat attacks. 35% on 2026-10-27; growth beyond 40% means new data is arriving with weaker dates.
Trend only.

The ASD risk matrix is published from stored classifications. The pipeline classifies before the dashboard phase, so more than 5% stale means classification was skipped or failed and the matrix describes events as they no longer are.
Count behind staleness.asd_stale_share.
Included in staleness.asd_stale; measurable on schemas without fingerprints.
Victim roles decided for a different membership; run `dedup_admin.py classify-entities --stale-only`.
Trend only.

Incidents with no usable victim role (186 of 1,090 on 2026-10-29). Not a finished classification: `dedup_admin.py fill-victims` gives them one at its calibrated threshold. Trend; the remainder are events whose evidence names no victim.
Facts (records affected, type) computed for a different membership; refreshed by the next deduplication.
evaluation/deployment_policy.json decides whether any calibrated step may act; without it every calibrated step raises rather than assume a rule, so the hygiene phase cannot have run as designed.

An automatic action whose calibration is current but whose labelled evidence does not pass the deployment rule (cyber_data_collector/dedup/deployment.py), or whose calibration is stale, is report-only. A warning, not a gate: report-only acts on nothing. The detail says what would satisfy the rule.
Trend: the exact lower bound on the action's precision on labels not used to choose its cut-off (scripts/evaluate_calibrations.py).
Trend: the exact lower bound on the action's labelled precision (unweighted and from the effective n, the lower).
Automatic actions held back by the deployment rule or a stale calibration; labelling more cases (or recalibrating) is what brings them back.

The recurrence analysis's 0-90 day band rests on a handful of repeats (4 on 2026-10-02); short-gap same-victim pairs are where reporting-lag duplicates concentrate. Above 10 the band is likely inflated by duplicates - run check-duplicates before trusting it.
Identical titles on two active events are usually one incident (or a generic title that identifies nothing).
One record counted as evidence for two active events double counts it.
Trend only.
Trend only.
An event with neither page text nor research cannot be verified or re-judged by the calibrated filters.
Count behind the share.
An unsupported event (no page text of its own, no validated research) has every field uncertain.
Exports and dashboards show the stored evidence_status; it must match the evidence.
Unsupported events no retrieval route can reach any more: review or reject by hand.

An item waiting for its first attempt for more than two weeks means the route is not being run (or is capped far below its queue): `discovery_queue.py refetch-cyberdaily --until-empty`, `dedup_admin.py recover-evidence --until-empty`.
Per-route queue progress (queued, attempted, succeeded, failing by failure type, exhausted), recorded every run for the trend table.
Unprocessed records older than 30 days are retries that keep failing.
Trend only.
Trend only.
processing_error values that are not filter rejections are unexplained failures.
Each quarantined enrichment needs a decision: fix and release, or accept the gap.
Trend only.
A month in which a monthly source delivered nothing, or under half its trailing median, is a collection gap.

A sharp fall in a source's events by event month is either a collection gap or reporting lag in recent months. CyberDaily is judged from 2026-11 (source_judge_from): its 2026-10 records are the one-off backfill to 2020, which would make every later month look short.

A Cyber Daily month whose search was given up on a permanent failure - the feed answered 404/410 - is never searched again, so its articles stay missing until someone looks. Fix, then `discovery_queue.py release`. Months that merely failed repeatedly are parked, not given up (backfill_months_parked).

Cyber Daily months that failed repeatedly for a temporary or unknown reason (retry_queue.MAX_SOURCE_MONTH_ATTEMPTS). They recover without a person - the source is probed on a schedule and they reopen on a successful probe or a configuration change - so this warns rather than blocks; their articles are missing until then. A month parked for weeks means the probe is failing: `discovery_queue.py status`.
Source-months given up on a permanent failure (404/410) are never searched again; each needs a decision, then `discovery_queue.py release`. (The Cyber Daily rule above blocks for CyberDaily.)
Source-months parked after repeated temporary or unknown failures recover by themselves (probe, or a configuration change); the count falling is the sign it is working.
Parked months whose source configuration has changed since: the next backfill, or `discovery_queue.py reopen`, searches them again.
A source's probe is the only thing that reopens its parked months on the schedule; overdue means the backfill that runs it has not run.
Records whose latest failure nothing recognised as the provider's or the record's fault. They are retried with a long back-off and never quarantined; the cause is in the log ('Unrecognised failure').

Stored confidence values whose provenance proves they were defaults (0.7 for an unscored event, 0.8 / 0.6 for the single-record path's entities). They read as model output: `python scripts/repair_confidence_defaults.py` sets them to NULL.
Trend only: values at exactly 0.7 / 0.8 that a real score can equal; nothing proves them defaults, so they are left as they are.
Trend only: enriched events with no confidence score. NULL means unknown and every reader treats it so.
The last search of these months lost results for a temporary reason (throttled, network, parse, other). The next run searches them again after a back-off, so this warns rather than blocks.
Months since 2020-01 Cyber Daily has never searched: its incidents for those months are missing. Run the backfill; months discovery has not processed are covered by normal discovery instead.
Trend only.
A completely searched month holding under half the articles of its neighbours means pages of the feed were skipped or articles were not stored. Check the month, then backfill --force it.
The feed listed more articles for the month than the database holds: storage dropped some.
Trend only; the retry queue drains these and backlog.raw_unprocessed_stale catches stuck ones.
Stories with cut-off or too-short page text were judged on a headline and standfirst. The re-fetch repairs a few hundred per run; the count should fall to zero.
Stories removed from the site (404/410) or given up after 5 failed re-fetches keep their stored text. Reported for review; `discovery_queue.py release` retries the given-up ones.
